I think that is an incorrect statement of the law, and I think you just have to go on a case-by-case basis but I'm sure that Your Honour didn't actually meant literally what -- what he said but merely that you have to look at the answers to the questions and then decide what if anything you will accept. But I think as an overall rule to say answers from leading questions are of little evidentiary value, if that is the case then I can understand why you don't want to have any cross-examination in court. And if that's the case then I guess we can just sit down and not do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't want to expand this discussion. I would like to go back to the starting point and to the issue of leading questions. I would like to remind you of the question put by General Praljak that the witness did mention that he was wounded at the time in the fights against Serbs, and although Praljak put his question within the context of the joint criminal enterprise and the overall circumstances of the beginning of the trial, I believe that this question had to do both with the direct and has a bearing on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honour, 15 seconds to respond to some minutes of the Defence. The fact -- the argument that an accused should be able to put evidence without any rules is a further argument for not allowing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, you could have easily dodged the issue because of which we've wasted 10 minutes. You could have asked the witness whether there were any military troops on the Hum hill. He would have said yes or no, and if he had said yes, you could have asked him what forces these were and he would have said the Serbs. So we've just wasted 10 minutes for absolutely nothing. Please proceed, Mr. Praljak, and please try to put your questions to the witness in such a way that these questions are not leading questions. I think you should succeed in doing that. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Your Honours. I did start my question with "Is this," or "Was it," and the witness could have easily answered me yes or no. I'll repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that the Yugoslav People's Army in 1992, in April, the fourth month of that year, was on the left bank and on the surrounding hills, that in town were reservists that on Hum, Orlovac, Stepcici [phoen], Slipcici were the positions of the JNA. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That is a classic leading question. You couldn't have put a better one than that. That is classic leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, but if Mr. Praljak is putting the question to the witness in that way it's because he wants to gain time. We all know that the JNA was stationed there. Please proceed, Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that the only road leading out of Mostar towards Western Herzegovina was via Ganovci [phoen].

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Are you aware of the fact that a large facility in Cule had been destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that a somewhat smaller transformation station [as interpreted] in Rastani had also been destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that around the 15th of May, 1993 [as interpreted], the Yugoslav People's Army and the reservists chased the entire population, this was in 1992, from the left bank the Neretva to the right bank of the Neretva?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I think there's a mistake in the transcript. I believe there is a mistake in the transcript or a misstatement by Mr. Praljak or one or the other. It says, are you aware of the fact that around the 15th of May, 1993, as opposed to -- I believe it was 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're absolutely right, Mr. Scott. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I put that right and said 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do know about that. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At the beginning of June 1992, an action to liberate the right bank of the Neretva was undertaken, Orlovac, Hum, et cetera, and further down, the aluminium factory, Sokol, that whole valley. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you also know whether in that operation the 1st Mostar Battalion particular part?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat that question? Do I know what?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In that operation did the 1st Mostar Battalion take part?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know the name of the commander of that operation?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to place the following document on e-court, 3D 00688. 3D 00688.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, have these documents been submitted to us or not, or are you just going to show them through e-court? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] 3D 00 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's on e-court, and we also provided a folder, a binder, at the end of the break. Judge Trechsel seems to have found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we've interrupted, let me say that there's an additional document without a number, but you'll realise that yourselves. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 3D 00688 is the number of the document I'd like to look at next. And you took part in the operation. It is it the operation to liberate the left bank of the Neretva River. And it says at the top the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the Croatian Defence Council, et cetera, et cetera. The Main Staff, the Operative Group, South-east Herzegovina. And that is the classical way in way an operation unfolds. Let us take a look. I'll read out some portions, and you can just tell me whether based on what you knew as a participant whether the document corresponds to the truth.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In your question a moment ago I didn't understand it that this was the left bank. You mentioned Orlovac and human those or on the right bank whereas this is a move to the left bank that I took part in as did the Mostar Battalion, the 1st Mostar Brigade, in fact, or, rather, the brigade I was in. So that's just a direction. We didn't understand each other. There was the Mostar Battalion there, and the unit that I was in, my company. So by way of clarification I'd like to say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, I said that it was at the beginning of June 1992, and then we moved on to a new topic, and we're now talking about the move to the left bank and the operation there, and you took part in it.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So let's go through a few things. Line 3: "Our artillery covered passages of our forces over the Old Bridge on the river Neretva." And then at 0650 hours: "The general ordered the artillery from Planica to constantly fire towards Balushani [phoen]." You know these geographical areas, do you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At 0720 hours the fighting took place in street by the cinema and around the opened bridge. At 0745 hours from South Camp there was firing at our forces once again around the Old Bridge. The general ordered Siroki Brijeg to go into operation near the Orthodox church and the detour there, and South and North Camp. At 0747 hours the tank moved along the main road, and that refers to the JNA tank; right, on the main road?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At 0810 hours, two tanks with infantry were moving from South Camp towards the town. That was the JNA again. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And at 0812 hours the enemy was firing at the old town and city. At 8.35 fighting allegedly began in Podvelezje but that was not confirmed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The chronology is very interesting in military terms because we have information about everything that is going on minute by minute. But what do you want to establish? Do you want to establish that 1st Mostar Battalion had the necessary resources? What are you trying to establish? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Please believe me, Mr. President, Your Honour, that I do have a purpose, and it will become clear in just a moment. I have a very clear objective.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At 0910 hours it says that the general ordered to the -- ordered the Independent Battalion, which is yours, to leave the bank and move forward. And so on. The general ordered snipers. The general ordered the Independent Battalion, et cetera, et cetera at 0958 hours. And then we'll skip some portions and go to 1100 hours, et cetera. Now, this operation, did it look like this roughly to the best of your recollections?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember this operation vividly, Mr. Praljak. However --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That will do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a soldier, an ordinary soldier carrying a rifle, and I don't know about this -- these companies and these orders. I crossed the Neretva River at Goranci.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. We've dealt with that that that's how it was. That's all I wanted to hear. And now my next question is this --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This is now mischaracterising the witness's testimony. Now, if Mr. Praljak is going to be allowed to put questions to the witness, then he should not mischaracterise, number one, the witness's testimony. Number two, he should give the witness a chance to answer. He's just said -- he's just now said the witness has confirmed what I put was right. The witness didn't say that. In fact, the witness said the contrary. I can't address all that. I was a foot soldier. I crossed the river. But Mr. Praljak then makes -- turns it into the answer he wants. That was not the testimony of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, the witness stated that he crossed the river. On that point he confirms what you're saying, but he was just a regular soldier and he's just told us that this was not something he was familiar with. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is this: To the best of your recollections, is this roughly what it looked like?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by roughly?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, the document that I've just put to you, can you confirm that that's how it was?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't confirm that. We did cross the Neretva River --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And there was an operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, the question was put and answered. You're not allowed to put it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, the witness answered your question. He said that he crossed the river, that an operation took place, but for the rest, whether there were armoured vehicles or if somebody was shooting with artillery, he cannot give you an answer to that. I don't know if this is of particular interest to you, but please ask him the question. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] All right. I completed that part of what I wanted to ask. I'm just going to go on and ask him the following:

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that in this operation that went from the south what the ratio of forces was, the HVO and the independent Mostar Battalion. What was the ratio of forces in this operation? How many men took part? How many soldiers did the HVO have, and how many soldiers did the independent Mostar Battalion have?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The independent Mostar Battalion numbered about 400 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. And now my question is this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Praljak. The witness has not answered the question. You asked for the relation. That is a comparison. Witness, do you know how many soldiers there were on the other side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now a question that goes to the heart of the matter in my opinion. Tell me, Witness, who is this general?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jasmin Jaganjac. I see his signature there, if that's it. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] So that is, Your Honours, why all this took place. And I have to put that on record. You've heard from other witnesses who testified here how important the operation was. Jasmin Jaganjac at that time was in Zagreb, and this other general, that was me, and that's my first point. Now I'm going to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Witness, of a single printed document, any paper, radio, information from 1992, June 1992, to the present day that at any time in any information media, public information media, in the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, whether they published who was in charge of the operation to liberate Mostar on the left and right bank? Was that ever published, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember it having been, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I think that that is what I wanted to get at, Your Honours, what truth is portrayed, what images are conjured up. May we have this next document placed on the ELMO. I have another question for the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document to be put on the overhead projector, let me ask you this, Witness: To the best of your knowledge, the Old Bridge, was it protected in the night between the 15th and 16th of June 1992 with planks and a special construction?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was protected, and we have photographs of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Right. Now, do you know the name of the man who ordered this to be done?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please -- the interpreters do not hear anything any more. Very well. Go ahead, please. Put your question, Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that in the might between the 15th and 16th of June, 1992, the Old Bridge was -- had planks placed -- a construction of planks placed over it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I have a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know how many men were engaged on the job that night?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the commander who ordered that this be done while the fighting was still going on nearby?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now take a look at the document on the ELMO. Can you recognise the handwriting as being that of Mr. Arif Pasalic? Take a look at the last page. You cooperated with him, so can you recognise that document of his and his signature?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recognise the document, but the signature corresponds to his signature, although I'm not 100 per cent certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now turn to page two, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, if might be useful if you were to tell us what kind of a document this is. I don't think you have so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, because we don't have the translation of this document on the ELMO, Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we went through it rather fast. Well, actually, we didn't manage to have it translated. It is a document which Arif Pasalic sends out, and it says "Commander." That's the title.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it does say "Commander." THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So Mr. Arif Pasalic, at the moment of writing this he is addressing a commander. Now, turn to page 2 and look at item 6. The third line. Read out to what says -- "It is necessary to check tomorrow the complete --" is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And it says: "Bringing in ammunition." Now let's move on to page 3 and look at paragraph 8. He says: "The Chetniks after the mortar fire," et cetera. Is that what it says, "the Chetniks"? Does it start off with "The Chetniks"?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And then paragraph 9 he says: "I kept the bridge under constant fire of heavy machine-guns. However, it was destroyed in the middle where you couldn't see the explosive, which indicates that the explosive was in the bowel of the bridge," et cetera. And it says that -- what they're talking about is Hasan Brkic bridge. Now, my question is this: Apart from the Old Bridge, to your knowledge, did the Yugoslav People's Army -- did it destroy all the bridges on the Neretva River in the same way?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what way, Mr. Praljak, you're referring to, but the Neretva is from Jablanica to Capljina and it lost 13 bridges, 11 railway bridges and two road bridges.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In that period, is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now turn to the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. President, perhaps Mr. Praljak could be kind enough to give us an approximate date for this document. If he said it I didn't hear, but we have no time or background on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, according to your sources was drafted by Mr. Vasilic [as interpreted]. On what date, please? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] In view of the destruction of the Hasan Brkic bridge, Your Honour, and the fact that we're talking about a military bridge, this occurred at the point in time when this operation that I spoke about was in place, the liberation of the left bank of the Neretva. And Mr. Pasalic at that time addressed a commander, and we'll see in due course later on who that commander was who he is addressing, and we're talking about the 15th of June, 1992, when we'd already crossed. There is mention of the airport and the bridge, and we know when this document was compiled and when all this was going on. And on the last page Mr. Pasalic is asking that he be sent a car and that he will receive other orders.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be allowed to say something? During the time when you're referring to when this document was compiled as you say, I was a foot soldier. I was not near the late Mr. Arif Pasalic, but there were very rare situations later on whereby he would write a document in his own handwriting without a date, without the usual kind of thing that a document has. So maybe this document was compiled under special circumstances. I wasn't in his vicinity. All I can say is that the signature might be Arif's, although I'm not 100 per cent certain of that. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Lizde, you're right. At the moment he was writing this Mr. Arif Pasalic was at the airport. This was an urgent message. He is asking for a car for ammunition and so on and so forth. I am asking you this: In view of the fact that you have already stated before it arises from this that in the month of June Arif Pasalic wrote to somebody addressing him as a commander. In other words, that there was a commander, that he had a commander. At that moment, according to what you know, did Arif Pasalic had a commander who was superior to him in the Independent Battalion in the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the -- Arif Pasalic was the main commander of the 1st Battalion of the BiH army. Now, whether I would be able to tell you whether the word commander refers to the army, to the HVO, to another unit, I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very, very well. We'll see that later. I'm just trying to --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In Mostar there was nobody else but the battalion but after the liberation of Mostar, according to what you know did the book under the title "Audited" become published?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And was it drafted together by Bosniaks and Croats. The book is Urbicide?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know exactly. It was published, but I don't know who authored it. It was a long time ago and I've forgotten. But, yes, the book Urbicide was published.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you had the book in your hands, would you say that it is an object representation of the devastation of Mostar at the hands of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Irrespective of who the author of the book was, whether it was Bosniaks or Croats or both of them together, no book, including this book Urbicide, could not reflect everything that had happened in Mostar at the time and later on I believe that book is only a partial confirmation of what happened in Mostar in 1992, especially on its left -- on the left bank of the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Are you saying that the situation was even worse?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was much worse.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: After that you were wounded at the foot of Mount Velez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes it was on the 30th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell me where you were hospitalised?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the Mostar hospital. That's how we call it, the new hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All of this time?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all this time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. And now since you were at the foot of the -- of Mount Velez, I would kindly ask you -- please, can this be put on the ELMO please, this document that I have in my hands?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, the document of Mr. Pasalic, is it on e-court? Is there a number for that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not yet. We will deal with that tomorrow, if we may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak has kept this document as an alternative awaiting the witness's examination-in-chief. He did not know whether he would use it or not but today because of the cross-examination and the questions that were put at the beginning of the cross-examination, he obviously deemed that he should use it and we will ask for its admission. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we now have document 3D 00732. Witness, you're familiar with Mostar, as well as I am. Can you use the pen to show us where the fighting took place at the foot of Mount Velez and where the lines of defence were later established between the HVO and the BH army on the one side and the JNA and the Republika Srpska army on the other side?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this map that you have just shown me?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I'm able to do that on this map. This map is not positioned very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You can see the airport in the left upper corner. On the left is Mount Velez.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see Blagaj on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Where do you see Blagaj on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see Blagaj on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I suppose that you're looking at a wrong map. Can you please remove this map from the -- from the ELMO and can we look at document number 00732. 3D 00732 is the document that I'm after. That is that and I don't have it on my screen. I don't have it on e-court. Now you can see Mostar very well. You can see the airport. You can see Blagaj. What about the defence lines between the BiH army and the HVO on the one side and the Republika Srpska army and the JNA on the other side?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only see Blagaj on one side in -- in Podumje [phoen]. I can see Blagaj and Gnojnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I have nothing. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, sir, the witness may not see it, you may not see it. Maybe the witness is not able to point at things here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, I can see Blagaj and Gnojnica as two places and below them I can see the hill, but I was on the left side at the foot of the -- of Mount Velez. I can't draw any lines. I can show you where I was and where the lines were in Podvelezje between upper and lower Bandalej [phoen]. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, sir, I understand that you are not a military person. You don't have military education but you can perfectly see airport here, Gnojnica, and you can see a hill leading up to Velez and you can see Podvelezje here. If you can't see it --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, maybe I can. I can -- I can try. Okay. I'll draw a line.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Try, please. As far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember that the lines were somewhere in the middle of Podvelezje.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Draw a line.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the green is Podvelezje, then this would be the line to the very end of Podvelezje, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could witness and counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think this simply doesn't work. The witness is now speculating. He's trying to be helpful and drawing lines but in fact it has become quite clear that his knowledge of the facts you're aiming at are very limited. He was at that time a soldier, as he'd said. You're asking of operative questions. The witness cannot directly testify on that. I think you should change the subject. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour Trechsel, you're absolutely right. However, we're faced with a problem here. You're absolutely right but we are faced with a problem. We get witnesses here who speak about the events that we had not discussed with any high officer of the BH army or an expert. We have not clarified any of these issues. So that's why we have to speculate with other witnesses about the Serb artillery, the number of soldiers. A year into the trial we are not aware of even the elementary facts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, I can tell you where I was wounded. I was wounded on the separation line and this is where I was wounded but my parents got -- friends got killed. But I can't draw it on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I just want to whole-heartedly join Judge Trechsel's comment. He doesn't need -- he certainly doesn't need my agreement to be right but in this case I certainly want to underline it. The point is that I'm not going to sit here and allow Mr. Praljak to blame his deficiencies on the witness's -- it's not the witness's fault. The witness comes to give particular evidence selected by the Prosecution to give certain evidence in the case that we believe is relevant to our case. We're not here to call evidence for Mr. Praljak. If Mr. Praljak doesn't think this is the appropriate witness, then he shouldn't put the questions to the witness then Mr. Praljak has just admitted he's wasting everyone's time. Everyone's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Praljak, the comment made by Mr. Scott is perfectly founded. We have before us a journalist, a reporter, and he had been arrested. He had been detained in various detention centres, and you are putting questions to him as if he had -- as if he was a general at the time. You're asking him to show us where the troops were and so on. It's the same as if you would ask a general questions on the work of a reporter. The general would tell you I'm a general, I'm not a reporter. So this is the difficulty we're all facing. However, the witness can maybe show us on this map the position where he was injured, because apparently he's able to tell us this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the green field is Podvelezje, then my line is okay, and this is where I was wounded on the 30th of June. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Very well. I admitted straight away and I've begin up on any further questions. I could not possibly know what the witness knows or what he doesn't know. So I'm giving up on this map. This is not a good line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you like to -- us to give an IC number for this map? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] There's no need for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I don't want to ask any more questions about your departure for Rama or Prozor. I'm moving on to the next topic. Do you know that I had two meetings with Vehbija Karic and Arif Pasalic after these events in Jablanica with the people who had ran away towards Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, can you be more precise? When did you have meetings?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: After the conflicts in Rama on the 28th of September, I had two meetings with Arif Pasalic and Vehbija Karic in Jablanica to deal with that problem. Are you aware of that as a journalist?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. My memory doesn't serve me too well on that. I can't remember any such meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that Mr. Vehbija Karic and Mr. Arif Pasalic were with me in Rama after that conflict? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that there was a meeting of the two delegations in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember meetings, but I can't tell you precisely where they took place and when, but I know that there were meetings. I'm aware of those.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The Ustashi hall that you saw as the inscription on one of the buildings in Rama, do you know that that was the headquarters of the HOS?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not on the building. This was on a white piece of cloth.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there were lads in camouflage uniforms and I didn't know who they were, whether they were HOS or HVO. They had red bands on their arms.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that the HOS was recognised by the Presidency of the Bosnia and Herzegovina and by Alija Izetbegovic as the regular army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that Blaz Kraljevic and Ante Prkacin, the HOS commanders, were recognised as generals by Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know something about that, but I would like to add something to that. Three days ago before I arrived here in -- we published a book by our journalist, an editor from Ljubuski, Mladen Bosnjak, and the title is Colonel or deceased person featuring the story of Mr. Kraljevic. So I know quite a lot from reading that book. I know quite a lot about Colonel Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that HOS was the army that advocated the political idea of the Party of Rights which was Croatia all the way to the Drina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very well known slogan. This is a notorious slogan.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And do you know that within the framework of the ideology of that army, there was also the fact that Bosniaks -- sorry, Muslims were also part of the Croatian people?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't understand what is the relevance of this question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poryvaev, I do see a relevancy. The witness was a reporter, and he told us that he had gone to Prozor. He told us that in Prozor he saw some people dressed in black, and they had red ribbons around their arm. The witness told us that those people belonged to the HOS. So that's the relevancy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I did not say that the men wore black uniforms in Prozor. They were in camouflage uniforms in Prozor, not black uniforms. And the inscription was Ustasha hall, and they had red bands around their arms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but what made you conclude that there was members of the HOS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... not say that they were members of the HOS [Realtime transcript read in error "Prosecution"]. I only said that the inscription on the building where they were was the Ustashi hall, and I never said that they were members of the HOS. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Can I ask the next question?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that the HOS continued --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's then, Mr. Praljak, who is going to ask you the question. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At the time, did the HOS advocate a large part the ideology of the Ustashi and they styled themselves Ustashi. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Since this was not entered into the transcript, do you know that their ideology, the ideology, the ideology of Ante Pavlovic was Croatia all the way up to the Drina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At page 21 -- excuse me page 68, line 21, the Prosecution has certainly been accused of a lot of things and probably will be in the future but I don't think any of these people were members of the Prosecution. If we could possibly have that corrected, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there is a mistake in fact. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The HOS had considerable troops, and according to them the Muslims were part of the Croatian people. Was that part of their ideology?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's very difficult to say that with certainty. There were individuals who thought that. I'm sure that there must have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that the only -- that when the bridges were destroyed that all the pipelines between east and west were so -- were interrupted?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mostar had problem with water. I don't know whether it was as a result of the destruction of bridges I suppose that it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that at the time an attempt was made to lay the pipes under the Old Bridge and that this was done very badly. The water leaked. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that at the time the manager of the public company waterworks in Mostar was Mr. Mustafa Zviznica?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zvizdic. It is possible but I don't know. I don't know who the manager of the waterworks was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, do you know anything about the document that has already been introduced dated the 3rd of January, 1993, according to which the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Ministry of the Interior, the plan of the physical security of facilities and the area around the Old Bridge, in one place it says as follows: The policemen are the points in the vicinity of the Old Bridge. In addition to the tasks that have been listed already are duty-bound to register all individuals who have crossed the Old Bridge and also to enter their residence. The reasons for which they are crossing to the left bank at the time when they have crossed over and returned from the left bank. In brackets the reference is made to civilians. Since the Old Bridge at the time was the only bridge between the eastern part and the western part, do you know that in January 1993 a complete control started of the civilians entering the left bank. The right bank was free at the time for movement, but whoever wanted to cross to the left bank had to be registered.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I do know that there were some checks, but you could cross the bridge at the dam as well. There were check-points. Now, who did the checking, I don't know. I think everybody was checked crossing the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: May I have 3D 00899 as the next document, please. 3D 00899. It's a statement dated the 13th of May, 1993 given by Mr. Dzemal Hamzic, son of Refik. You know the man?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: He gave this statement to the police station in Mostar, and it relates to the radio station that you were the director of -- of which you were the director of the political and information programme.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't the director.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, editor then.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, editor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In a radio station under wartime conditions, an editor of the information and political programme is the number one man, the most important man of that radio station.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he's a fairly important man, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now would you take a look at what it says here? He says -- when he was offered the job of establishing that radio station he said: "I had previously held consultations with Tomo Mazalo and asked instructions from him whether I would have any adverse consequences for my future work within the frameworks of the information station of Mostar," et cetera, et cetera. "And then I was offered to establish and being an editor of a paper called Mostarsko Jutro which I accepted and I was given a letter of credit from the defence department of the HVO HZ HB." Then he says that he was the editor-in-chief of the War Radio Station Mostar, and then he goes on to say that the War Radio Station Mostar had its programme board which included Dzevad Kolukcija, Izudin Sahovic, Arif Pasalic, and others. There was Father Ivan Sevo representing religious organisations and humanitarian organisations at the end. It says with regard to the establishment of the war studio the main object was that the information put out be true and correct, but it collided -- that collided with Arif Pasalic because the man wanted to influence me with respect to editorial policy. And I clashed with him over that. And then he goes on to say that this gentleman tried to relocate the Mostar studio from those premises because there was a great deal of influence brought to bear on editorial policy, and then he says: "To the best of our ability we made it impossible for Arif Pasalic to disseminate his propaganda on the airwaves," et cetera. Now, Mr. Arif Pasalic, was he able to turn up at any time of day or night and be broadcast over Radio Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he couldn't come. He came when he was invited by me. He never came otherwise. Well, everybody could do everything like Dzida. As Dzida came Arif could have come too. But he didn't. And this is a notorious lie that Dzemo has set out here. This is the first time that I'm seeing this. He didn't have an occasion to be on good terms or bad terms with Arif Pasalic. Everything that Arif wanted went through me. Dzemo Hamzic wasn't on good terms with me and I don't suppose he was on good terms with Arif Pasalic either.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You yourself gave a statement, and you said that you gave Mr. Vidovic a statement and signed it, and it is a document from the Prosecution file, and you say the following on page 2 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: What number did you say?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It is a Prosecution document. I'm going to read your statement out and then you can testify. "As far as the relationship between the BH army is concerned and the war radio station, I can say that some people from the BH army such as Arif Pasalic, for instance, had the advantage of being able at any time to coming to the radio and state what they wanted." That is what you say on page 2 word or word in your statement.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I said that that was the only statement that I signed. I gave the statement on one day and they gave me the statement to sign the next day. I didn't read what it said in the statement and that was at the central prison in Heliodrom, and I would like to ask you to understand the circumstances under which I signed it, and I only saw this for the first time the other day. They could have written whatever they wanted. And would you have signed had you been in a camp for two months? You would have signed anything that they handed to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Lizde --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that. That wasn't the statement I made.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I didn't say anything else. I just read it out. You say that you didn't. You say no.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you of the circumstances and how I came to sign that statement. I explained that to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I just have a couple of other questions. Could this be placed on the ELMO, please, this next document, so that the witness can see it. And I'm going to ask you this in the meantime: Before the conflicts in Mostar, conflicts had happened before that in Konjic. Did you or your journalists -- Mr. Lizde, I'm speaking to you. You or your journalists, a little before the conflict started, did you report -- give out any reports about the events in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were reports from Konjic. It -- they were written about and talked about but I don't know what you mean specifically.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I don't have time to show you the crimes that were committed in Konjic, but, for instance, did you ever broadcast over the radio the events that occurred in Trusina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: When did these events occur in Trusina?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You don't know when?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of the events Trusina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: After the 16th of April, 1993, after that date did you broadcast anything about the 23 men that were killed in Trusina let alone all the rest of it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now, would you place the next document on the ELMO, please. This is a diagram of -- showing Santic Street, Spanish -- the Spanish Square, the Celovina prison and so on. Is this a relatively good sketch of the area?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me have a look. Let me take a moment to study it. I don't know if you have time, but I'd like to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we zoom down a little. Can we see the whole diagram? Zoom out so we can see the whole of it.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, roughly that would be it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I lived in Santiceva for two years, and opposite Celovina. It's a broad street five metres wide and there's a pavement two metres wide on each side; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the usual type of thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And do you know that the trenches were dug where the concrete was or were the lines here from one street to -- from one house to another?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was from one house to another, from one window to another.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, the building that is circled was the association of drivers and mechanics. Were you there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was in the Kragujevac restaurant building.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you indicate where that building was located?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, can I see the whole diagram?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's hotel Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, hotel Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Would you draw that on the map, please, then? Indicate where it is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I just want to state, not only did we not receive this document either, we do not know where it comes from. We only see an exter [phoen] where there is no circled house. This is not very helpful, I must say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's where I was, where I drew the circle. At the corner of hotel Herzegovina, whatever. What does it say here.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says ZTU. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Would you put a number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Well, I'm sorry, Judge Trechsel, but I had to draw this overnight because the witness made the statement yesterday. So I can't draw all these maps and diagrams before I hear what the witness says. So I'm asking the witness whether this corresponds to the area and he said yes, so I've done the best I could. I don't know what else I could have done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You could have told us it was a plan you had drawn last night. That would have been helpful if we had known from the outset where this had come from. Now you have told us. Thank you. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I apologise. I thought that that was obvious, that it was drawn last night.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you now tell me whether the HVO was at the top of Santic Street and down the bottom of Santic Street, the BH army?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, can we zoom down, see the bottom half. At the entrance to Santic Street it says, "The MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina." The bottom line, it says, "MUP RBiH."

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. That wasn't the MUP. I know that it was a supermarket. It's the Merkur supermarket. If you lived there you knew that the Merkur supermarket was there. I didn't know it was ever the MUP. How could I know that?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Lizde, it's very simple. You don't know that the MUP was there and that solves the problem. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that the MUP was down there, that was the Merkur supermarket.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now when you went to Jablanica you remember saying that you went to Jablanica for some negotiations?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to SpaBat headquarters or, rather, UNPROFOR headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you take the asphalt road Mostarjit [as interpreted] to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Any problems along the route?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were stopped at the 5th Battalion check-point on a bridge in Aleksin Han, before the Aleksin Han bridge. Well, yes, the road -- there was a check-point on the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me, you were referred to as Brada, beard, because you wore a beard. Some people referred to me as Brada too. Is it customary that everybody who has a beard tends to be referred to as Brada. How many -- what would the percentage of people be?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew another Brada, beard, who was a waiter in Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So they called him Brada?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did but that weren't that many people with beards.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, I assume that's why they referred to them as Brada. Now I'm sorry that I can't go into all this in greater detail but I'm satisfied with what I have so far. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I really think that to clarify technical matters such as these diagrams which afterwards can show us whether a sniper can shoot from such-and-such a building where the lines were, whether they were two metres apart or 20 or 30 metres apart, that this contributes to elucidating the truth that you need to find, just as it contributes to the truth of my question, "Do you know who commanded the operation?" You heard that there was a major operation at the beginning of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, if a journalist doesn't know who that was, then one can draw the conclusion of how much propaganda there was which failed to disseminate information as to who the general was, who was in command of the operation, and I think that this will help throw light on what is important in this case, where the lines were in Podvelezje. If the witness says that the Serb artillery couldn't shoot other than the areas it did, then what can I do? I have to show where the front lines were in Podvelezje and where the Serb artillery was. And afterwards, did they shoot at Mostar with diminished intensity after that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question to ask. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] You'll have to ask the Judges whether you can ask your question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Opposite where the drivers were, that's where the army was, the BH army, and that was the road that was the separation line. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, then put the number 2 there and say the BH army.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then you'll see that it was two metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The BH army and the HVO. Number 1, HVO, and number 2 put the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now we have the following procedure which the Judges always ask for. Write down the date and your signature and ...

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I write in Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You can write whichever way you like.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I don't see what it -- that I'm doing anything bad. I'm not taking up time. I'm seeking the truth. I'm seeking out facts. And please, in that respect I don't think Mr. Scott is right in what he says. I think I am proceeding in a perfectly proper manner. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can you please give us a number for this map?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this map will be IC 530.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm now going to give the floor to Mr. Kovacic, who needs a few minutes. Mr. Registrar, can you please tell me how much time has been used up by the Defence so far and how much time has been used by Mr. Praljak? I'm looking at the clock right now. We might be able to finish today. It's just a possibility, but we still need to hear Ms. Alaburic. Mrs. Alaburic, how much time will you need?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will depend on the quantity of information that this witness can offer, but I believe that it will take me between 15 and 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Tomic, how much time would you need? MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have my own 36 minutes, and if I need extra time, I've been given 10 minutes by my colleague, Nozica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. We might be able to complete the testimony of the witness by 7.00 p.m. Mr. Kovacic, you have the floor now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I believe that I won't need more than 10 minutes. The witness is cooperative. He wants to assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Lizde.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I would like to follow up on our discussion that we had yesterday about the alleged sighting of Mr. Praljak at the Heliodrom. Let's start with the claim. Yesterday you told us three times that somebody else had told you that in the group of people, and you thought that it was a delegation of sorts, that there was also Mr. Praljak. For the record.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the record, these claims were on page 55, lines 12 and 13, page 56, lines 17 to 20, and page 57, lines 1 to 3. Mr. Lizde, could you please try and remember who it was who said that to you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were 10.000 people at the Heliodrom together with me, and I really can't remember. Somebody who was with me at the time told me that but I can't remember who it was. I don't know where I ate three days ago, let alone this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please try and remember where the -- there was just one person who said that or were there several people who said the same thing?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think that several people were involved. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you also told us that the group of people among whom Praljak allegedly was you saw only briefly, and I am quoting you and even if you -- if I had known Praljak at the time I would not have been able to recognise him. You said this on page 57, line 24, and on page 58, line 4.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Let me just put the question to you. First of all, did I quote you correctly? Did I quote exactly what you said yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. As I sit here today, I believe that the Prosecution asked me a wrong question. The question was whether I saw somebody at the Heliodrom or in the building where I was incarcerated. Heliodrom, as somebody correctly said it, is a large space, a lot of squares metres. I did not see anybody in the building where I was incarcerated. And there were delegations passing by every day, and I saw a lot of delegations passing through Heliodrom and I didn't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'll come to that. Mr. Lizde, let's take things a step at a time let's take one answer after the other and we'll come to that let's go back to the beginning of this discussion. You said that the sighting was so fast you would not have recognised Praljak even if you had known him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: It rises from that, and my question is logical, can you explain how come the person who had told you that they had seen Praljak could recognise Praljak in such a brief moment?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that his perception was better.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you think that person must have had a better view or a better situation from which he was observing?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Further on you said that you don't remember when this was, whether this was during your first stay at the Heliodrom or during your second stay at the Heliodrom. I don't want to quote the transcript pages again. You've told us that you were incarcerated at Heliodrom on two occasions, the first time in July between -- in June between the 15th and the 25th [as interpreted], and then in mid-July until the moment you were released.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You have mentioned bars again today, and you mentioned the same bars yesterday. Let me try and jog your memory. During your first incarceration at the Heliodrom you were incarcerated in the prison building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In that building were there bars on the windows?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. During your second visit or, rather, incarceration in July and later on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Kovacic. I note a small inconsistency. Yesterday, the witness has stated that he stayed at Heliodrom until the 30th of June. Now you have put to him until the 25th, and he has said yes, but I don't know whether he wants to change the statement or whether there was maybe a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can't see that on my screen, but it must be a mistake in the record. I mentioned the 30th, and the witness confirmed that date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 30th of June, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I have distinctly heard the 25th, and you read it on line 16, but it's okay now. It's good that it's rectified. Maybe it was a translation error.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: During the second period of time when you were incarcerated the add Heliodrom and further on you were at the school building if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I was in the hall and then in the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you remember when you were in the hall and the school there were no bars on the windows?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the classical prison bars, but there were also bars. There were windows on the third and the fourth floors and on the ground floor the windows were improvised and we did not have a good view from the windows. In the -- in the school I was on the first -- on the ground floor and in the hall there were also classical window bars. And the feeling was the same. I remember that very often I wished to be able to breathe fresh air without the bars in the school and in the hall. I didn't have a good view. This is what I meant when I said bars. They were not classical bars, to be precise, but there were bars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this lengthy explanation, but I don't want you to go into such great detail. We don't have that much time. I need to finish. Can we then conclude -- excuse me, allow me put the question. Can we then conclude from what you've just told us that the detail about the bars did not help you to jog your memory?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Can I then conclude that you still do not remember not even roughly when you saw that group?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You have told us spontaneously that the group of people that we are talking about was not passing between the buildings that were used as prison.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prison was a system of building -- across the road from the school was the lead brigade of Tigers from Zagreb. The central -- the prison was not encircled. The central building of the prison was some hundred metres from the school and across the road from the school was the -- where the Tigers from Zagreb were billeted and behind them were the Thunders from Split, Osijek, and so on and so forth. There were also buildings that were destroyed. They were not all in use.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Don't go into great detail.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to explain. The prison was not like the prison in Santiceva. It was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let's summarise. While you were there, you knew exactly which of the buildings that you have just mentioned as having been located at the Heliodrom, and there were many of them, and you knew exactly which buildings were used as prison?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You didn't?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I only knew about the building where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You've -- and you've mentioned those.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The group that you mentioned, did they come to any of these buildings that were used as prison?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know they didn't. I'm sure that they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well then. Could you please tell me whether you know the name of the warden of the Heliodrom prison?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stanko Bozic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And his deputy?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not know before I saw this document. I didn't know at the time who the warden was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When I tell you that his family name was also Praljak, would you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't. I don't know anything about that. It doesn't ring any bells.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Are you sure that the person who mentioned the name Praljak at the time was not referring to the deputy prison warden Praljak?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but there was an additional sentence, and the sentence was to the effect, how come you don't know him? He's from Mostar as well. I did not know who the deputy warden was I didn't even know who the warden was until I saw the document which said that I was being released from prison and the document was signed by Mr. Stanko Bozic. I don't know that there were many comments about Praljak as being the deputy prison warden. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Just one more question about this, Witness. The person who has mentioned Praljak's name as the person being in that group did not provide any description of that Praljak, didn't mention his position, description, or any such thing?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: But since this was a high-ranking delegation and people who were passing by through that complex that there were a lot of soldiers around them, I don't think one could speak about the prison warden or the deputy prison warden being escorted by so many soldiers. We did not comment upon that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Just maybe one more question and we will come to the end of this topic. You have provided a total of three official statements after the war. First between the 10 and 12 April, and then in June 2002 [Realtime transcript read in error "1992"] to the investigator of The Hague Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And then you provided another additional statement on the 16th of January, 2004, again to the investigators of the Prosecutor's office; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In addition to that -- actually, the first statement that you provided was to the military police of the 4th Corps of the BiH army on the 7th of March 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will we agree then that nowhere in these statements except in the first one given in 2002, did you mention the story about having seen Praljak at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the question? What am I supposed to agree with?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: That only in the first statement dated 2002 you mentioned that fact.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will we agree that your memory was better in 1994 when you provided the first statement?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Not necessarily so. But if I remind you that in the 2004 statement on page 24 of the Croatian text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the Judges, on page 15 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You stated that the event when you saw that delegation took place in the second part of June 1993. Was your memory so much better in 2002 that it is today?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I -- I don't know. I can't be sure even now when this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it then true that you still adhere by the fact that you still don't know, despite the fact that you've mentioned a certain period of time in one of your statements?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there are some things in the transcript that are not correct and it's probably a result of this big speed that you have. If you look on page 87, you have -- 86, line 19. Mr. Kovacic asks about the statements, and then you are quoted as saying: "First between 10 and 12 April and then in June 1992." You must have meant or even said 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right, Your Honour. I did say 2002, because I was looking at the date on the statement. This is the statement that was taken over the two days of April and two days of June in 2002, the same one that you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I add another sentence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would first make another correction. On page 87, line 4 and 5, a statement provided to the military police of the 4th Corps of the BiH army on the 7th of March, 1994? Is that -- is that correct? Is it a statement to the -- to the 4th Corps of the BiH? Because I have here the statement of the 3rd Military Police Battalion of the HVO on 12 June 1993. But you did not want to refer to that one, I think. That would be the first statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, according to what I have in my file, the date is 7 March 1994, and the -- in the heading you can see the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the 4th Corps, the battalion of the military police, which means that the statement was provided to the military police of the 4th Corps. And this is a document that I was provided by the Prosecution, and I believe that you must have it because we were provided with the same documents from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I do have it, Mr. Kovacic, but I have an earlier one. So the first one perhaps would have been an earlier one. But if you did not want to refer to it, you don't want to refer to it. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This was enough to me. This is one of the statements that was given very soon after the events when one might expect from the witness to still remember the events very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I say one sentence? I would like to say the following to Mr. Praljak: In my office on my radio at the moment there is a photo of a tank shell hitting the Old Bridge in 1992, which had come from the positions in Podvelezje. This is something that I'd forgotten to say, but I believe I have to say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to object. Yes, this is the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a shell that came from Podvelezje in 1992. I have this photo. It sits in my office and it shows how the Old Bridge was damaged on that occasion. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I was saying, it's half past 5.00. We'll have a 20-minute break now. We'll resume with Ms. Alaburic and Ms. Tomic, and theoretically we should be able to complete the testimony of the witness today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lizde, good afternoon. Tell us to start off, Mr. Lizde, when radio Bosnia-Herzegovina, the war station -- war radio station in Mostar, when was it established?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th of September, 1992, if I remember directly. In 1992, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Before the beginning of broadcasts, were consultations held with other beneficiaries of radio frequencies and whether an agreement was reached of any kind with respect to frequencies, the frequencies you'd be broadcasting on?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If I understood it correctly, when the radio station was established you were the assistant commander of the 4th Corps of the BH army for information and propaganda; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LIZDE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you a few questions which have to do with your work as assistant commander of the 4th Corps for information and propaganda, and to start off with I'd like to ask you to look at the set of documents you received. There are only two documents. We can look at them together, and I'll be drawing your attention to what will be the important points as far as my questions are concerned. The first document is 4D 00036, and it is a report by Arif Pasalic, dated the 2nd of May, 1993, and I'd like to ask you to look at the bottom of the first page and focus on point 3, and we can look at the second line together where it states: "Our people with -- we have carried out linkage with our people in the HVO." And then on the next page, line 5 from the top it says: "The people from the HVO of Capljina have the task of taking control of the village of Popovcici and the bridge at Capljina with the aim of preventing forces being brought in from Metkovic."
